page: Microsoft Azure D48alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Daldsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture, offering 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 2835 GB NVMe SSD and supports Premium Storage.

In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates strong performance characteristics. The AMD EPYC processor achieves a Passmark CPU score of 77885.39, with strong results in extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests. Single-threaded compression and decompression are highly efficient, with gzip compression reaching 41.5 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression reaching 18.1 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10% tier. Memory performance is highlighted by a cached read-only small block bandwidth of 5011.43 GB/sec. For database operations, the server handles 77.15 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 28576.08 on Passmark database tests.

The instance is capable of handling lightweight machine learning tasks, delivering top-tier prompt processing speeds of 4366.28 tokens per second and text generation speeds of 397.95 tokens per second for small 135M parameter LLM models. However, performance drops to average levels when processing larger 70B parameter models due to the memory-to-core constraints. Given its high compute density, fast local NVMe storage, and strong database benchmarks, the D48alds_v7 is well-suited for compute-heavy workloads, static web serving, high-throughput database operations, and localized data processing tasks that do not require massive memory footprints.
description: Microsoft Azure D48alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Daldsv7 family, powered by a dedicated 48-vCPU AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, it features 96.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core) and a bundled 2835 GB NVMe SSD. The server exhibits strong performance across various benchmarks, including a Passmark CPU score of 77885.39 and top-tier single-threaded gzip compression at 41.5 GB/sec. It also delivers strong database capabilities, processing 77.15 million Redis SET operations per second. While highly efficient for compute-dense tasks, its low memory-to-vCPU ratio represents a tradeoff for memory-intensive applications. This configuration is best suited for high-throughput web serving, database operations, and compute-heavy workloads.
